description: Labelled golden dataset for the retrieval ranking stages (fusion + rerank + assembly). Each case supplies what the two storage arms would return for a query — the ranked candidate lists — plus the chunk ids a human judged relevant. The SQL arms themselves are covered by tests/retrieval/integration; this set exists to measure the ranking logic we own, deterministically and without a database or an embedding provider.

corpus.content: Invoices are issued on the first day of each billing period and are payable within 14 days. Usage overage is billed in arrears on the following invoice.
A failed payment moves the subscription to past_due. Three retry attempts are made over ten days before the subscription is cancelled.
Plan changes are prorated to the second. Downgrading refunds the unused remainder of the current period as account credit, never as a cash refund.
Refund requests are accepted within 30 days of the original charge. Refunds are returned to the original payment method and settle in five to ten business days.
Annual plans are refundable on a pro-rata basis for the unused months. Monthly plans are refunded in full only within the first 30 days.
SSO is available on the Enterprise tier. SAML 2.0 and OIDC are both supported, and just-in-time provisioning creates workspace members on first login.
Audit logs record authentication events, permission changes, and destructive operations. They are append-only and retained for one year.
Each workspace has a monthly agent-run quota determined by its subscription tier. Exceeding it returns HTTP 429 with a quota_exceeded error code.
Rate limits are applied per workspace and per API key using a sliding window. The retry_after field tells the client when to try again.
Create a workspace, build an agent from a template, then run it. Most teams reach a first successful run in under ten minutes.
